recipes.description: Install Portainer, then hand all HomeLab containers to your Docker manager. LMS stops managing them.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Install Portainer CE on this host. Keep it on the direct network and show its local URL. When it is healthy, hand all HomeLab containers, including Portainer, to the Docker manager. I will manage their lifecycle and configuration there and complete administrator setup in Portainer.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Confirm the Docker socket exists and verify the local endpoint. Successful deployment transfers every HomeLab container to Docker-manager ownership, including the manager itself. LMS will not install, start, stop, repair, update, remove, or recreate containers after handoff. Import saved Compose files into the manager when replacing existing containers.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Keep Docker administration on a Tailnet for private remote access, or the LAN for local administrators.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route to reach image registries and the Docker host; no VPN client gateway is needed.

recipes.description: Install Arcane, then hand all HomeLab containers to your Docker manager. LMS stops managing them.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Install Arcane on this host with a generated protected encryption key. Keep it on the direct network and show its local URL. When it is healthy, hand all HomeLab containers, including Arcane, to the Docker manager. I will manage their lifecycle and configuration there.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Confirm the Docker socket exists and verify Arcane's local endpoint. Preserve the generated encryption key when migrating Arcane. Successful deployment transfers every HomeLab container to Docker-manager ownership, including the manager itself. LMS will not install, start, stop, repair, update, remove, or recreate containers after handoff.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Keep Docker administration on a Tailnet for private remote access, or the LAN for local administrators.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for image registries and managed Docker hosts.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Confirm the Docker socket exists and verify Dockhand's local endpoint. Successful deployment transfers every HomeLab container to Docker-manager ownership, including Dockhand itself. LMS will not install, start, stop, repair, update, remove, or recreate containers after handoff.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Keep Docker administration on a Tailnet for private remote access, or the LAN for local administrators.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for image registries and managed Docker hosts.

recipes.description: Plan Komodo Core, its database, and Periphery together before transferring Docker ownership.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Plan a Komodo deployment using its official Core, database, and Periphery setup. Check the host architecture, database choice, persistent storage, local access, and agent connection. Do not install a partial stack or hand off existing HomeLab containers during planning.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Komodo requires a database and a Periphery agent to manage this host. LMS does not currently have a complete Komodo stack recipe. Produce a reviewable deployment plan using Komodo's official Compose files; do not claim Komodo is installed or that LMS ownership has changed.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Keep the Core administration UI on a Tailnet or trusted LAN; plan agent access separately.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for Core, its private database, agents and image registries.

recipes.description: Install Dockge, then hand all HomeLab containers to your Docker manager. LMS stops managing them.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Install Dockge on this host. Keep it on the direct network and show its local URL. When it is healthy, hand all HomeLab containers, including Dockge, to the Docker manager. I will manage their lifecycle and Compose stacks there.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Confirm the Docker socket exists and verify Dockge's local endpoint. Its Compose stacks live at the host path declared in the app catalog and mounted at the same path inside Dockge. Successful deployment transfers every HomeLab container to Docker-manager ownership, including the manager itself. LMS will not install, start, stop, repair, update, remove, or recreate containers after handoff.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Keep Compose administration on a Tailnet or trusted LAN.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for Docker image registries and local Compose workloads.

recipes.description: Plan a private Ollama and Open WebUI server with hardware-aware acceleration.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a private local AI server with Ollama and Open WebUI. Detect my available GPU and ask which model sizes and access policy I want before deployment.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Confirm CPU-only, NVIDIA, AMD, or other acceleration and available memory. Do not claim GPU support until LMS can validate the runtime and device mapping.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local model clients and Open WebUI; choose a Tailnet if only private remote clients should connect.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for model downloads and local model-server traffic.

recipes.description: Plan a local coding assistant with a web UI, code models, and controlled Git access.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up an AI coding box with Open WebUI, Ollama, suitable local code models, and Git integration. Ask which repositories, languages, GPU, model size, and Git permissions I want.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Treat repository access and Git credentials as protected configuration. Do not choose a model or grant write access without the user's requirements.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a Tailnet or trusted LAN to keep the coding UI and repository access private.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for repositories, model downloads and development dependencies.

recipes.description: Plan a private Forgejo service with PostgreSQL and an explicitly registered runner.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a private Forgejo Git platform with PostgreSQL and a runner. Ask about the hostname, storage, runner workloads, registration token flow, and external access before deployment.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep PostgreSQL private. Register the runner only after Forgejo is healthy and never place its registration token in chat.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a Tailnet for private repository access, or a trusted LAN; keep the database private.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for runners, Git remotes and dependency registries.

recipes.description: Plan a browser-based development environment with Git and chosen language SDKs.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a disposable code-server development environment with Git. Ask which language SDKs, versions, extensions, repository access, persistence, and resource limits I need.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Do not guess the SDK image or persist Git credentials in the container definition.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a Tailnet or trusted LAN for the browser-based development workspace.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for Git remotes, SDK downloads and package registries.

recipes.description: Set up Webtor and Stremio behind one reusable VPN Gateway, with LMS-managed local access and streaming connectivity.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up Webtor and Stremio behind an existing VPN Gateway with LMS-managed local access. Ask me which gateway to use if there is more than one.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Preserve distinct shared-namespace ports and use the generated Webtor client endpoint for browser-facing integration. Use only personal, public-domain, or otherwise lawfully accessed content; do not configure content sources or add-ons.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for playback clients. The listener stays reachable locally while app outbound traffic uses the VPN.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use an existing VPN Gateway for Webtor and Stremio outbound traffic; local playback access uses the chosen listen address.

recipes.description: Create a Jellyfin library with Seerr, Radarr, Sonarr, Prowlarr, and qBittorrent, while routing automation through Gluetun.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a complete local Jellyfin media library with Seerr, Radarr, Sonarr, Prowlarr, and qBittorrent. Keep Jellyfin local, route the automation services through one existing VPN Gateway, and reuse LMS-managed downloads, movies, and TV storage.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Never route Jellyfin through Gluetun. Give each routed service a distinct listener and report both LMS local URLs and shared-namespace loopback endpoints. Do not select or configure indexers, catalogues, download sources, or content.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN so TVs, browsers and media clients can reach Jellyfin and the local service UIs.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use a VPN Gateway for qBittorrent, Prowlarr, Sonarr, Radarr and Seerr. Jellyfin stays on the normal direct route for LAN playback; it is not routed through the VPN.

recipes.description: Plan a Navidrome music library with an optional lawful download and import pipeline.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up Navidrome for my local music library. Ask about storage, metadata, users, external access, and whether I want an authorised download or import pipeline.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep the library persistent and do not invent content sources. Treat the optional pipeline as a separate choice.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local music players; choose a Tailnet for private remote listening.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for the music server. Decide any optional download pipeline routing separately.

recipes.description: Set up Immich with its managed PostgreSQL, cache, and machine-learning services.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a private Immich photo and video library with persistent storage, database, cache, and machine-learning services. Ask about storage and access requirements not already configured.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Verify every managed dependency and the LMS local access route before reporting the library ready.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local photo uploads and browsing; choose a Tailnet for private remote devices.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for photo clients and any model or metadata downloads; managed dependencies stay private.

recipes.description: Set up qBittorrent behind a reusable VPN Gateway and verify its traffic cannot bypass the gateway.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up qBittorrent behind an existing VPN Gateway and store downloads in LMS Home Lab storage.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Inbound port forwarding is optional. Preserve the LMS route and verify VPN security.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for the qBittorrent management UI; its download traffic is a separate outbound choice.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use an existing VPN Gateway for qBittorrent outbound traffic. The LAN listener does not bypass VPN routing.

recipes.description: Run Bitmagnet as a private torrent indexer and DHT crawler with persistent PostgreSQL storage.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up Bitmagnet behind an existing VPN Gateway with its managed PostgreSQL database in the same network namespace. Use the internal Bitmagnet Torznab endpoint from Prowlarr if you want to add it as an authorised indexer.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Bitmagnet indexes torrent metadata and does not download media itself. Keep it private, configure a personal TMDB key or disable TMDB integration, and only use sources and content you are authorised to access.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a trusted LAN for the private indexer UI and local automation clients.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use an existing VPN Gateway for Bitmagnet and its required shared-namespace database.

recipes.description: Set up qBittorrent, Prowlarr, FlareSolverr, Sonarr, Radarr, and Seerr behind one VPN Gateway.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up qBittorrent, Prowlarr, FlareSolverr, Sonarr, Radarr, and Seerr behind one existing VPN Gateway.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Use distinct shared-namespace listeners. Configure Prowlarr to use FlareSolverr at the generated internal service endpoint when an indexer requires it. Do not select or configure indexers, catalogues, download sources, or content.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local access to the automation UIs, even though their outbound traffic uses a VPN.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use one existing VPN Gateway for qBittorrent, Prowlarr, FlareSolverr, Sonarr, Radarr and Seerr.

recipes.description: Create a standalone Jellyfin server for locally hosted movies and television.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up Jellyfin for local network streaming from LMS-managed movies and TV storage.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep Jellyfin direct, with read-only media mounts, and verify its local route.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN so TVs, browsers and other home media clients can stream from Jellyfin.

recipes.description: Create a local Jellyfin library alongside Sonarr and Radarr.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up Jellyfin with Sonarr and Radarr using LMS-managed movies and TV storage.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for Jellyfin playback and local Sonarr/Radarr administration.

recipes.description: Plan a WireGuard server for secure access to the home network.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a private WireGuard VPN server. Ask about the LAN subnet, public endpoint, DNS, client count, router forwarding, and whether the host is behind CGNAT.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Do not confuse a WireGuard server with the existing outbound Gluetun VPN Gateway.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN-facing interface for the WireGuard server listener; plan router forwarding explicitly for clients outside the LAN.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route to reach home-network destinations. A WireGuard access server is not an outbound VPN client gateway.

recipes.description: Plan a WireGuard exit node split between this server and a chosen VPS.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a WireGuard VPN exit node using a VPS. Ask which VPS, operating system, public address, routed subnets, DNS, and client platforms I use.
recipes.technicalGuidance: This spans an external machine. Separate local LMS work from VPS commands and require the user to confirm the remote target.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN-facing interface for the local tunnel endpoint; confirm which interface and address the chosen VPS can reach.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Plan the exit route through the chosen VPS explicitly. Selecting direct here does not create that exit tunnel or choose its physical interface.

recipes.description: Plan network-wide DNS filtering with AdGuard Home or Pi-hole and Unbound.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up network ad blocking. Ask me to choose AdGuard Home or Pi-hole, then plan Unbound, a dedicated LAN address, router DNS changes, upstream policy, and recovery DNS.
recipes.technicalGuidance: DNS must bind the correct LAN address and port 53 without colliding with the host resolver. Do not deploy both front ends.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN address that household devices will use for DNS; keep the administration UI private.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route to reach upstream DNS resolvers and update sources.

recipes.description: Plan a private Headscale control plane and enrolment of Tailscale clients.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Client enrolment and auth keys occur after the control plane is reachable; never place reusable keys in chat.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN address for the Headscale control-plane listener, then plan the hostname and remote-client reachability.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for client coordination and any relay connections; do not route the control plane through an unrelated VPN Gateway.

recipes.description: Plan Caddy or Traefik routing with certificates and an explicit exposure policy.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a reverse proxy. Ask me to choose Caddy or Traefik and provide domains, internal targets, certificate method, authentication, and exposure requirements.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Inspect LMS Caddy and Edge Gateway first to avoid duplicate bindings on ports 80 and 443.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN-facing address for local upstream access; plan public listeners and port forwarding separately.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for upstream services and certificate requests.

recipes.description: Plan Home Assistant with MQTT and Zigbee device integration.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Hardware discovery may require host networking or explicit devices. Validate the adapter before deploying Zigbee2MQTT.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN so Home Assistant can serve household clients and integrate with local devices.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for local devices, MQTT and any cloud integrations.

recipes.description: Plan Frigate with MQTT and validated GPU or Coral acceleration.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the camera LAN interface for Frigate and local viewing; select the camera VLAN if this host has separate networks.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host routes to cameras and MQTT. A VPN Gateway is not required for local camera traffic.

recipes.description: Plan energy collection and dashboards using Home Assistant, InfluxDB, and Grafana.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN shared by local energy devices and dashboard clients.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for device integrations and private time-series services.

recipes.description: Plan Nextcloud with a private database and Redis cache.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep the database and Redis private and separate application data from database backups.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local sync clients, or a Tailnet for private remote devices; plan any public hostname separately.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for sync clients and configured integrations; the database and cache stay private.

recipes.description: Plan device-to-device file synchronisation with Syncthing.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Do not expose the admin interface publicly and do not share device IDs beyond the intended peers.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local file-sync peers; choose a Tailnet if peers should connect only over your private remote network.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for sync peers and any configured discovery or relay services.

recipes.description: Plan Restic or Borg backups with an optional MinIO object target.

recipes.technicalGuidance: A backup is not complete until a restore test is defined. Keep repository keys out of chat.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a Tailnet for private remote backup clients, or the LAN when all clients are local.

recipes.description: Plan a private MinIO-compatible object store.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a trusted LAN for object-storage clients, or a Tailnet for private remote access.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for storage dependencies and configured replication targets.

recipes.description: Use Immich as a private photo and video library.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Verify all managed dependencies and explain that cloud export/import remains a separate user-authorised step.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local photo uploads and browsing; choose a Tailnet for private remote devices.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for photo clients and optional model or metadata downloads.

recipes.description: Plan Nextcloud as a private file sync and sharing service.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up Nextcloud as my Google Drive replacement. Ask about storage, desktop and mobile clients, sharing, office integration, backups, and external access.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep its database and Redis private; do not claim existing cloud data has been migrated.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local file-sync clients, or a Tailnet for private remote devices.

recipes.description: Plan a private Vaultwarden service with backups and secure external access.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Prefer a Tailnet for private vault access, or a trusted LAN. Plan HTTPS and any external access explicitly.

recipes.description: Plan a private metasearch service using SearXNG.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Use a persistent secret key and do not expose an unrestricted public instance by default.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a trusted LAN or Tailnet for the private search UI.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route to search providers. If a VPN is wanted, confirm provider compatibility and supported routing during planning.

recipes.description: Plan privacy-focused web analytics with Umami and PostgreSQL.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep PostgreSQL private and do not add tracking code to sites without explicit instruction.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for the analytics listener, then plan which websites need to reach its collection endpoint.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for configured integrations; keep PostgreSQL private.

recipes.description: Plan a personal web archive using ArchiveBox.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up ArchiveBox. Ask about archive storage, import sources, crawl depth, browser dependencies, schedule, users, and access.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Estimate storage and respect site permissions and applicable archiving rules.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a trusted LAN or Tailnet for browsing and administering the personal archive.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route to fetch the sites being archived.

recipes.description: Plan a private FreshRSS feed reader.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up FreshRSS. Ask about users, imports, refresh schedule, authentication, storage, and external access.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep scheduled refreshes reasonable and protect external access.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local RSS-reader access, or a Tailnet for private remote reading.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route to retrieve RSS feeds and configured integrations.

recipes.description: Plan a private Stirling-PDF toolbox.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Treat uploaded documents as sensitive and avoid public anonymous exposure.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a trusted LAN or Tailnet so document-processing access remains private.

recipes.description: Plan Paperless-ngx with database, cache, OCR, and document storage.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep database and Redis private and validate writable document paths.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a trusted LAN or Tailnet for document uploads, search and administration.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for configured mail/import sources; database, cache and OCR dependencies stay private.

recipes.description: Plan a private BookStack knowledge base.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep the database private and preserve both uploads and application keys.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local readers, or a Tailnet for private remote access.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for configured mail and other wiki integrations.

recipes.description: Plan service monitoring and a status dashboard with Uptime Kuma.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up Uptime Kuma. Ask which services to monitor, check intervals, notification channels, status-page visibility, storage, and external access.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Do not place notification secrets in chat and avoid publishing internal target details.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for the monitoring dashboard; plan any public status-page access separately.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route so probes can reach the intended LAN and Internet services. A VPN changes the network path being monitored.

recipes.description: Plan scheduled connection tests and history using Speedtest Tracker.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up Speedtest Tracker. Ask about schedule, server selection, retention, notifications, timezone, storage, and external access.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Avoid an excessive test schedule that distorts bandwidth use.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for the connection-history dashboard.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route to measure this host connection. A VPN would measure the VPN path instead.

recipes.description: Create WordPress with its managed database and persistent site files.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a private WordPress website. Let me specify a version, variant, database choice, administration tool, domain, or other requirement.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep the managed database private and explain unsupported variants before applying.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for initial site setup; publish the site through the chosen gateway or proxy separately.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for plugin/theme updates and configured site integrations; keep the database private.

recipes.description: Create a private Squid forward proxy for networks the user controls.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a private forward proxy for devices on networks I control.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Choose the LAN or private interface whose clients may use Squid, then choose the outbound route. Direct uses the server's regular LAN/Internet route; VPN sends proxy traffic through the selected VPN Gateway. Configure each client with the reported proxy IP and port. Do not expose it through Edge Gateway or any public route because that would create an open proxy.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a trusted LAN address reachable by the intended proxy clients; choose a Tailnet for private remote clients.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for proxied destinations. Review access policy and any desired VPN routing explicitly.

recipes.description: Run FlareSolverr as a private helper for indexers that need Cloudflare challenge solving.

recipes.technicalGuidance: Keep FlareSolverr private and configure the client with the generated internal FlareSolverr URL. Use it only with services and sites you are authorised to access; do not expose it publicly.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use a trusted LAN reachable by the indexers that need this helper; do not publish its API openly.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route, or select a supported VPN Gateway if the consuming indexers use that route.

recipes.description: Plan a RomM library with browser emulation.

recipes.technicalGuidance: The user supplies lawfully obtained game files and any metadata credentials through protected fields.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local game-library browsing and browser emulation.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for configured library metadata and integrations.

recipes.description: Plan a private LANCommander game library.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up LANCommander as a private game store. Ask about library storage, users, authentication, game imports, and LAN-only or remote access.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Do not source or distribute game files; the user provides authorised installers.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN for local game downloads and launcher clients.
networkRecommendation.outboundReason: Use the normal host route for configured game-library sources and local clients.

recipes.description: Plan Sunshine streaming with Moonlight clients and validated graphics hardware.
recipes.baseRecipePrompt: Set up a Sunshine cloud gaming server for Moonlight clients. Ask about GPU, display session, audio, input devices, games, network, resolution, and remote access.
recipes.technicalGuidance: Validate hardware encoding, display access, and host device mappings before deployment.

networkRecommendation.listenReason: Use the LAN-facing interface for low-latency Moonlight clients; plan remote streaming separately.
